tasks.short: Set equipment and staffing capacity for loading, unloading, movement and storage.

steps.what: Review expected receipts, dispatches, stock movements and workload peaks.
Combine shift availability, equipment capacity and handling standards into a capacity worksheet.
Check congestion, equipment condition and practical handling constraints with the warehouse supervisor.
Compare overtime, shift changes, equipment rental and workload smoothing.
Choose staffing and equipment levels within budget and safe operating limits.
Record the agreed plan and distribute equipment and staffing requirements.

tasks.design: A scheduled calculation on the {DATA_PLATFORM} combines workload from the {OPS_SYSTEM}, aggregate shift availability from the {HCM}, and equipment records. It generates constrained capacity scenarios in the {BI}; after the manager approves a plan, the {WORKFLOW} records and distributes it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Workload, equipment and shift data sit apart. Local handling assumptions make a generic capacity calculation unreliable.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding lowers the cost of connectors, scenario calculations and validation. Capacity arithmetic needs no model loop.
tasks.still_hard: Congestion, breakdowns and safe operating limits need local observation. Aggregate capacity does not establish who can safely perform each job.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise unsafe or impractical plans and negotiate workable changes with supervisors.

ambition.what: Daily overtime-versus-equipment-rental decisions during demand peaks.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time assembling capacity worksheets and more time checking floor constraints. Existing staffing and spending authority remains unchanged; daily scenario review becomes practical.

reach.task: Translate dispatch peaks into handling capacity requirements.
reach.learn: Handling standards, bottleneck analysis and shift-level demand profiles.

reach.task: Compare equipment rental with repair or replacement.
reach.learn: Equipment availability, maintenance constraints and total operating cost.

evidence.claim: Aggregate workload and capacity scenarios can use deterministic calculations; floor feasibility remains a human judgement.
Build ranges are planning estimates, not measured implementation results.

assumptions: This describes aggregate capacity planning, not automated assignment or scoring of individual workers.
The manager can approve plans within existing spending limits; larger commitments follow existing approvals.
GDPR applies to personal data. Any extension into worker allocation or monitoring needs EU AI Act assessment and consultation under applicable national rules.
The access range allows initial employee consultation where required; formal national procedures may take longer.
unknowns: Availability and quality of workload, shift and equipment data.
Local handling standards and safety constraints.
Existing approval limits and applicable consultation procedures.
research_questions: Which aggregate workload measures best predict congestion at the relevant handling areas?
new_work: Maintain handling standards, equipment rates and capacity limits.
Investigate missing workload data and scenario infeasibility.
Compare planned capacity with actual throughput without introducing individual performance scoring.

tasks.short: Coordinate purchasing, material planning, inventory, warehousing and receiving through daily exceptions.

steps.what: Review stock, shortages, open receipts and warehouse workload.
Reconcile operations status with purchasing exports and identify exceptions.
Agree shortage priorities, receiving capacity and recovery owners with operational teams.
Approve replenishment proposals and purchasing changes within delegated limits.
Read supplier messages and record revised dates, quantities and unresolved conditions.

loop.input: Supplier message thread and matching purchase order.
loop.output: Proposed order-linked dates, quantities, conditions and source quotations.
loop.check: Validate order and line identifiers, units and date formats; flag conflicting or conditional statements.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per thread; missing references or unresolved conflicts go to the manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Supplier prose contains conditional promises and inconsistent date expressions that field mappings cannot reliably interpret.

steps.what: Resolve delivery conflicts and negotiate recovery commitments with suppliers.
Check recovery progress and chase overdue internal actions.

tasks.design: Connect the {OPS_SYSTEM} and {PROCUREMENT} through the {DATA_PLATFORM} to maintain an exception queue and replenishment proposals. A bounded extraction loop turns supplier messages from the {EMAIL} into proposed updates for review, while the {WORKFLOW} routes purchasing approvals and tracks recovery commitments.
tasks.previous_blocker: Stock, purchasing and supplier updates use different identifiers and refresh cycles. Managers bridge them through exports, messages and meetings.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing planning configuration handles routine replenishment. Cheaper connector development and bounded text extraction reduce the remaining coordination work.
tasks.still_hard: Supply promises can be unreliable. Scarce-stock allocation, strategic purchases and supplier negotiations still require commercial judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Set priorities across competing teams and secure credible supplier commitments.

ambition.what: Daily reorder overrides for volatile items.

tasks.altitude: The manager works from a current exception queue and spends more time resolving shortages. Purchasing authority remains unchanged; the manager can revisit volatile-item replenishment decisions daily.

reach.task: Investigate stock discrepancies before they distort replenishment.
reach.learn: Stock transaction trails, unit conversions and receipt reconciliation.

reach.task: Tune replenishment parameters for unstable demand.
reach.learn: Lead-time distributions, forecast bias and service-stock trade-offs.

evidence.claim: Slim4 provides item-level forecasting and stock planning.
The Lasaulec vendor case reports improved inventory and availability outcomes; it does not establish savings for this design.
Cross-system exception reconciliation and reviewed extraction of supplier updates are feasible implementation patterns.

assumptions: Purchasing and stock records have usable order, item and location identifiers.
Purchasing changes take effect only after the relevant delegated approval.
Supplier correspondence may contain personal data; GDPR access, retention and minimisation requirements apply.
The design does not score employees or allocate their work; changes to that scope require EU AI Act assessment and applicable national consultation.
unknowns: Extent of shared identifiers and timestamp consistency.
Supplier message volume, languages and ambiguity.
Purchasing approval thresholds and mailbox access.
research_questions: Which exception thresholds minimise alert fatigue without hiding material shortages?
How reliably can conditional supplier promises be extracted from representative message threads?
new_work: Review extracted supplier updates before they change planning records.
Maintain item mappings, replenishment thresholds and approval routing.
Resolve stale data, duplicate exceptions and overdue recovery actions.
Sample extraction errors and adjust validation rules.

tasks.short: Choose economical transport routes and shipment consolidation options.

steps.what: Review shipments, delivery windows, loads and warehouse dispatch constraints.
Check contracted transport rates, carrier capacities and service restrictions.
Compare routes, consolidated loads and alternative distribution points.
Confirm unusual delivery constraints and carrier feasibility with dispatch.
Select routes and consolidation changes against cost, service and disruption risk.
Release the approved route plan to dispatch.
Compare actual transport cost and service with the selected plan.

tasks.design: Feed shipments and validated rate tables into the routing module of the {OPS_SYSTEM}; configure capacity, delivery-window and consolidation constraints. The manager reviews feasible scenarios before release to dispatch, and the {BI} compares planned cost and service with actual results.
tasks.previous_blocker: Routing tools can already optimise loads, but incomplete constraints and disconnected rate data leave managers comparing scenarios manually.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing optimisation software handles route search. AI-assisted coding makes rate imports, constraint validation and actual-versus-plan reporting cheaper to connect.
tasks.still_hard: Customer flexibility, carrier reliability and warehouse consolidation costs can be poorly recorded. Moving distribution capacity requires a separate investment decision.
tasks.human_edge: Judge when a cheaper route threatens service or creates an operational dependency.

ambition.what: Weekly flexible-delivery consolidation offers for small customers.

tasks.altitude: The manager reviews costed alternatives and spends less time rebuilding route comparisons. Route approval authority stays the same; a customer-facing consolidation service would need a separate commercial mandate.

reach.task: Validate route feasibility before dispatch release.
reach.learn: Delivery restrictions, loading sequences and driver-hours constraints.
Network modelling, handling costs and sensitivity analysis.

evidence.claim: The Carrefour Poland sponsored case describes reducing kilometres per pallet through route planning.
Route scenarios can be generated by constrained optimisation without a language model.

assumptions: The existing {OPS_SYSTEM} includes a licensed routing module; otherwise deterministic optimisation needs a larger build.
Warehouse consolidation scenarios use existing sites and capacities, not automatic facility closures.
Only approved route plans are released internally; carrier booking follows existing authority.
GDPR applies where routes contain personal data. Individual driver allocation or monitoring requires separate EU AI Act assessment and applicable national consultation.
unknowns: Routing module availability and supported constraints.
Accuracy of dimensions, rates, delivery windows and address data.
Carrier booking responsibilities and dispatch approval rules.
research_questions: How much planned consolidation survives realistic warehouse and carrier constraints?
Which customers value flexible delivery enough to support a consolidation offer?
new_work: Maintain rate tables, delivery restrictions and routing constraints.
Investigate infeasible plans and actual-versus-plan variances.
Monitor optimisation runtime and mapping-data costs.
Develop commercial terms and capacity limits for any consolidation offer.

tasks.short: Define supply chain metrics, calculation rules and targets for cost, quality and service.

steps.what: Agree which business decisions and supply chain outcomes the metrics must support.
Inspect available fields, data coverage and existing calculations.
Specify formulas, denominators, exclusions, reporting grain, owners and proposed targets.
Backtest candidate metrics and examine sensitivity, missing data and misleading incentives.
Approve metric definitions and targets with affected operational owners.
Publish approved definitions and update dashboard calculations.

tasks.design: Keep versioned metric definitions in a records app on the {WORKFLOW}, linked to governed fields on the {DATA_PLATFORM}. Deterministic checks generate coverage and sensitivity reports; after approval, validated definitions update the catalogue and calculations in the {BI}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Definitions live in documents while calculations live elsewhere. Repeated data checks consume analyst time, but agreement on meaningful measures remains a management responsibility.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding reduces the cost of a metric registry, reusable validation routines and controlled publication. No model loop is needed for explicit formulas and templates.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing fair comparisons, defensible exclusions and useful targets remains difficult. A precise metric can still reward the wrong behaviour.
tasks.human_edge: Choose measures that reflect real service and cost trade-offs, and challenge incentives that encourage gaming.
tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time checking calculation consistency and more time discussing trade-offs and incentives. Metric approval rights remain unchanged; target reviews can use fresh evidence each month.

reach.task: Test whether proposed metrics support the intended decisions.
reach.learn: Measurement validity, sensitivity analysis and incentive effects.

reach.task: Define comparable quality measures across suppliers and sites.
reach.learn: Defect taxonomies, sampling limits and denominator consistency.

evidence.claim: Metric registries, formula checks and backtesting can use deterministic software.
Defining useful metrics requires judgement beyond automating dashboard production.
Build ranges assume a limited initial metric catalogue and accessible historical data.

assumptions: Metrics describe supply chain processes, products, sites and suppliers rather than individual employee performance.
The initial build uses an explicit formula vocabulary and a limited set of governed datasets.
GDPR applies wherever personal data enters the datasets. Extending metrics to employee evaluation requires separate EU AI Act assessment and consultation under applicable national rules.
The high automation prior is reduced because defining measures and agreeing targets remain substantial parts of this task.
unknowns: Existing metric catalogue, data dictionary and calculation ownership.
Historical data quality and comparability across sites.
Who approves targets that affect other functions.
Whether any proposed metrics evaluate identifiable workers.
research_questions: Which candidate metrics change decisions rather than duplicate existing reporting?
Which exclusions or denominators create unstable comparisons or incentives to game results?
new_work: Review validation findings and approve definition changes.
Maintain field lineage, formula versions and historical comparability.
Investigate data drift and unintended incentives.
Retire measures that no longer support a named decision.

role.altitude: The supply chain manager moves from assembling planning inputs to reviewing constrained alternatives and resolving operational trade-offs. Existing approval rights remain; broader investment or commercial authority needs explicit delegation.
reach: Logistics analyst: compare capacity, routing and inventory scenarios using validated data.
Production planning clerk: connect material and dispatch schedules to handling capacity.
Management analyst: test whether metrics improve decisions and avoid harmful incentives.
skills_to_grow: Data lineage, validation and exception design.
role.ambitious_version: Run a weekly integrated capacity, stock and transport review that selects costed recovery options before shortages threaten delivery commitments.
